To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the relationships between compositional and mechanical tissue properties are age-dependent; (2) non-linear interactions between composition and mechanics provide better discrimination than linear interactions; and (3) a few combined compositional and nanoindentation measures provide better classification than a single measure.

the tissue-level compositional (Raman) and mechanical (nanoindentation) properties are significant determinates of skeletal integrity and that non-linearly combined Raman and nano-indentation metrics provide a more comprehensive assessment of the tissue-level properties than a single metric.

tissue-level composition and material properties in cortical bone are highly interrelated and that a few non-linearity-based compositional-mechanical metrics provide better discrimination of specimens than a single metric.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the key determinants of bone tissue-level properties and how they change with age.
understanding how compositional and mechanical tissue-level properties change with age, and how they may interact to affect bone material integrity.
the development and implementation of a data mining approach to identify compositional and mechanical variables that can be used to classify bone specimens into groups based on age.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

age-specific patterns in tissue-level mechanical and compositional bone properties are complex and non-linear, and that non-linear multidimensional analysis of tissue-level composition is necessary to identify metrics that best discriminate bone specimens of different ages.

the tissue-level compositional properties and mechanical properties are significantly different between young and old bone and that these differences can be best described by a combination of compositional and mechanical variables.
the tissue-level mechanical and compositional changes in bone occur in a complex and nonlinear fashion, and that these changes are not independent of each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tissue-level mechanical properties and compositional properties of cortical bone are not simply linear functions of age, rather, they change in a complex and non-linear manner.
the tissue-level mechanical and compositional changes with aging are complex and non-linear.
the tissue level composition and mechanical properties are significantly altered with age and these alterations are complex, non-linear and cannot be captured by linear correlation analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of compositional and mechanical measures provides a powerful tool for understanding the complexity of age-related changes in tissue-level properties in skeletal tissue.
a combination of spectroscopic and mechanical measures provides better discriminatory information than either technique alone.

the combination of spectroscopic and nano-indentation data provides a powerful tool for understanding bone tissue properties and for identifying potential mechanisms of age-related changes in bone mechanical properties.
